# Retrospective: t2-12973-53d6149c

## What worked

- Opus's runtime harness with the earlier head as a positive control made both "resolved" dispositions concrete, and two sealed replicates matched.
- Neutral cross-examination after both finals turned a single-sourced mechanism (Qt per-URL error cache, `Qt.clearComponentCache` absence) into an independently confirmed claim. Sol's follow-up also corrected an overstatement in its own final about retry after errors.
- Reviewers converged on the same pre-existing re-entrancy window from different directions (Sol source, Opus synthetic run).

## Process deviations

- `pi_job.py status` (and `wait`) output includes a `latest_text` field. Checking Sol's lifecycle after exit showed the coordinator Sol's one-line conclusion before the Opus final existed. Not disclosed to Opus. Suggested tool change: add a `--lifecycle-only` flag or omit `latest_text` from status until the coordinator opts in.
- A 10-minute Sol check timer ran to completion after Sol had already exited; harmless.

## Friction

- Node.js is absent inside the review.py sandbox, so repository node test blocks needed a shim and QML-engine evaluation. Consider adding node to the sandbox tool set.
- No compositor fixture for Wayland layer surfaces; the issue's end-to-end symptom stays out of reach for command-only review.

## Carry forward

- For "Fixes #N" PRs, ask reviewers explicitly whether the change addresses the linked issue's mechanism, not only the review claims. Here that question produced the most useful new finding.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12973#issuecomment-5787692658) of `2ff6664c`, checked at `2c1c92a5` in response to the [author's update](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12973#issuecomment-5804378019). **Verified:** both earlier findings are resolved. Separately, the linked issue's symptom (#12959) is not shown to be fixed by this revision.

| Earlier finding | At `2c1c92a5` |
|---|---|
| Duplicate service instances during asynchronous loading | Resolved |
| Host parenting granted by a self-declared `clonedFrom` name | Resolved |

**Verified:** In an offscreen Quickshell 0.3.1 check using the extracted loader from each revision and synthetic services:

```text
                                   2ff6664c (earlier)        2c1c92a5 (current)
two syncs while compiling          2 instances per service   1 instance per service
disabled or removed while loading  instance published        not published
clone / fake-clone service parent  serviceHost               detached (same as base)
```

Re-enable, rescans with replaced manifests, a changed entry point, reload, load errors and a `createObject()` failure also ended with one instance or none, and no stuck pending claim. In the same offscreen check, a detached service shaped like `Background.qml` still created its window; a real Wayland layer surface was not tested.

## The linked issue's symptom is not shown to be fixed

In the same synthetic check, a service whose entry file was missing on its first load logged `service plugin load failed for <id>: file:///<plugin dir>/Service.qml: No such file or directory`. After the file was created, the next sync logged the same error again. This occurred on base, the earlier head and the current head:

```text
first load, file absent   -> Qt caches the failed load for that URL
file created              -> later createComponent(url), either mode -> same cached error
shell plugin reload       -> Qt.clearComponentCache is undefined in QML, cache kept
```

In Qt 6.11.2 source, the missing-file check and the per-URL cache of the failed load are the same for `Component.Asynchronous` and `Component.PreferSynchronous`. The [cache-clear guard in `finishPluginReload()`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/2c1c92a57e433aed743bed5865721d760e933745/shell/shell.qml#L1524) never runs, because `Qt.clearComponentCache` is not a QML method (it is on the C++ `QQmlEngine`). For `omarchy.background`, the clone command already copies the whole plugin directory, so the new `ensure_entry_points()` check does not change that clone.

**Impact:** The issue's report (the error repeating while `Background.qml` exists, and the original plugin still working) matches a cached failed load for the clone's URL, which neither the asynchronous switch nor the clone check affects. What made the file unavailable at the first load was not determined, so `Fixes #12959` is not supported by the evidence found.

**Suggested change:** Reproduce the clone in a real Quickshell session, logging the first load's resolved URL and whether the file is visible at that moment, and identify that trigger before relying on `Fixes #12959`. If a cached failed load is confirmed, recovery needs a new cache key or a fresh engine (for example a full shell restart) rather than another `createComponent()` call on the same URL; these options were not tested.

**Optional test improvement:** The new loader coverage checks the pure `claimCurrent()` helper and source regexes, not `ensureService()` or `_syncServices()` behavior. The new background clone assertions also pass against the base clone command, so they do not detect this PR's change. A behavioral loader test driving repeated syncs and disable/reload during compilation would cover the new claim logic.

**Optional:** `finalize()` clears the pending claim right after `createObject()`, before `shell` and other properties are injected and before the instance is stored. In the synthetic check, a service whose property-change handler triggered a sync during injection produced a second instance on all three revisions, so this is pre-existing, and no current built-in service has such a handler. Clearing the claim after publication (for example in a `try`/`finally`) would close that window.

**Test scope:** Source review of the current head, Qt 6.11.2 and Quickshell 0.3.1 source, plus isolated offscreen Quickshell 0.3.1 checks using the extracted production loader from base, `2ff6664c` and `2c1c92a5` with synthetic services and modeled registry events. The repository's clone and auth-boundary tests were run without a compositor, so the auth test's runtime section was skipped. No Wayland compositor, real background layer surface, live clone of `omarchy.background` or original issue trigger was tested.
